current.text: Toronto traded Brandon Ingram and added Kawhi Leonard.
Usage moves to Kawhi Leonard and away from RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley.
With Kawhi Leonard in, a usage jump for Scottie Barnes is harder to get.
Projected starters are Immanuel Quickley, RJ Barrett, Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Jakob Poeltl.
The expected closing five is Quickley, Barrett, Leonard, Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles. It is a small, switchable group, so Murray-Boyles closes games instead of Poeltl.
Poeltl is the only seven-footer on the roster.
The team is not deep. After a solid top seven, the rest of the rotation is Jamal Shead, Allen Graves, Kyle Anderson, Elijah Martin and Trayce Jackson-Davis.
Sean predicts 52 wins, or 56 to 57 wins if Kawhi Leonard plays 75 games. The market win total is lower at 45.5.
Toronto is possibly a top-four team in the East, so tanking or late-season shutdowns look unlikely.
The defense was top five to seven last season and is expected to hold or improve.
Toronto is fairly close to done with roster moves after the Kawhi Leonard trade.
Toronto has 15 back-to-backs, a middle-of-the-pack number.
Toronto plays 11 games in our fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21, among the most in the league. That helps its regular starters.

tags.detail: 11 games in weeks 19 to 21 (rank 4 of 30), with 1 back-to-back each in weeks 20 and 21

tags.name: thin rotation
tags.detail: Solid top seven, then Shead, Graves, Anderson, Martin and Jackson-Davis
tags.new_meaning: The team has few reliable players beyond its main rotation, so its starters and top reserves get heavy minutes.

tags.name: contender
tags.detail: Sean predicts 52 wins and calls them possibly a top-four team in the East
tags.new_meaning: The team expects to win many games, so tanking and late-season shutdowns of healthy players are unlikely.

note: Kawhi Leonard takes over the usage that Brandon Ingram had, so expect lower roles for RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley, and a usage jump for Scottie Barnes looks less likely. Toronto plays 11 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, among the most in the league, and it looks like a contender with a thin bench, so its starters and Collin Murray-Boyles should get steady minutes late in the season. Early on, watch how minutes split between Jakob Poeltl and Murray-Boyles, since Murray-Boyles is expected to close games, and watch how many games Kawhi plays.
